value: 薬屋のひとりごと (Kusuriya no Hitorigoto)
text: The Apothecary Diaries is Kusuriya no Hitorigoto in Japanese, a title that can be read as Apothecary's Soliloquy.
excerpt: The Apothecary Diaries (薬屋のひとりごと, Kusuriya no Hitorigoto, lit. Apothecary's Soliloquy) is a Japanese light novel series

value: Hyūganatsu (story); light novel illustrated by Touko Shino
text: Hyūganatsu is the author of the story, and Touko Shino draws the illustrations of the published light novels.
excerpt: a Japanese light novel series written by Hyūganatsu and illustrated by Touko Shino

value: Web novel on Shōsetsuka ni Narō since 2011; Shufunotomo light novels from August 29, 2014, 16 volumes by May 2025
text: The tale began as a web novel on Shōsetsuka ni Narō in 2011, then Shufunotomo issued a single book in 2012 and a Hero Bunko light novel line from August 29, 2014, which had 16 volumes by May 2025.
excerpt: In 2014, Shufunotomo began to publish the series again, illustrated by Touko Shino. This time, it was published as a light novel in their Hero Bunko imprint

value: Monthly Big Gangan (Square Enix), art by Nekokurage, from May 25, 2017, 17 volumes
text: Square Enix publishes the first manga adaptation, drawn by Nekokurage, in Monthly Big Gangan; it started on May 25, 2017 and has reached 17 volumes.
excerpt: The first is published by Square Enix in Monthly Big Gangan with art by Nekokurage

value: Maomao's Notes on the Inner Palace: Minoji Kurata, Shogakukan, Monthly Sunday Gene-X, from August 19, 2017
text: A second manga take, drawn by Minoji Kurata for Shogakukan's Monthly Sunday Gene-X, launched on August 19, 2017 under the title Maomao's Notes on the Inner Palace.
excerpt: the second is published by Shogakukan in Monthly Sunday Gene-X with art by Minoji Kurata

value: Toho Animation Studio and OLM, directors Norihiro Naganuma and Akinori Fudesaka, 24 episodes, October 22, 2023 to March 24, 2024
text: Toho Animation Studio and OLM made the first season together, and its 24 episodes ran on Nippon TV from October 22, 2023 until March 24, 2024.
excerpt: Produced by Toho Animation Studio and OLM, the series was written by Norihiro Naganuma and directed by Naganuma and Akinori Fudesaka.

text: Season two returned on January 10, 2025 and ended on July 4, 2025, adding episodes 25 to 48 to the total of 48.
excerpt: a second season was announced. It aired from January 10 to July 4, 2025, on Nippon TV's Friday Anime Night and its affiliates.

value: Premiered October 2, 2026, produced by OLM alone, in two parts
text: Season three started on October 2, 2026 as an OLM-only production, carries on from episode 49, and plans its second part for April 2027.
excerpt: a third season was announced that premiered on October 2, 2026. The season, now produced solely by OLM, will run in two parts

text: The story takes place in an invented empire modeled on Tang-era China, although the author points out that it is technically not set in China.
excerpt: Set in a fictional country inspired by Tang Dynasty-era China, the series follows Maomao, a girl trained in medicine by her apothecary father.

text: Counting the light novels and both manga series, the franchise had more than 57 million copies in circulation by August 2026.
excerpt: By August 2026, the franchise had over 57 million copies in circulation.

value: OP 1: Hana ni Natte - Ryokuoushoku Shakai (season 1)
text: Season one started with Hana ni Natte and Aikotoba, then switched to Ambivalent by Uru and Ai wa Kusuri by Wacci.
excerpt: The initial opening theme song was "Hana ni Natte", performed by Ryokuoushoku Shakai; the ending theme song was "Aikotoba", performed by Aina the End.

value: ED 3: Shiawase no Recipe - Dai Hirai (season 2)
text: Season two opened with Hyakka Ryōran by Lilas Ikuta and later Kusushiki by Mrs. Green Apple, with Dai Hirai and Omoinotake singing the endings.
excerpt: The first opening theme song is "Hyakka Ryōran" (performed by Lilas Ikuta) and the first ending theme song is "Shiawase no Recipe", performed by Dai Hirai.

value: OP 5: Kumo o Nukekazashimo e Watashidake - Yorushika (season 3)
text: The third season pairs an opening by Yorushika with the ending song AIYOU by Eve.
excerpt: The first opening theme song is "Kumo o Nukekazashimo e Watashidake" (performed by Yorushika) and the first ending theme song is "AIYOU", performed by Eve.

text: No source names story arcs, so this quiz follows the three anime seasons, with the third still on air in October 2026.
excerpt: The first season ran from October 22, 2023, to March 24, 2024, on Nippon TV and its affiliates.

value: Maomao (猫猫): the apothecary sold into the palace as a servant
Jinshi (壬氏): the influential official of the rear palace
Gyokuyō (玉葉): the Precious Consort, the emperor's favorite
Lakan (羅漢): the monocle-wearing military tactician
Lihaku (李白): the soldier who gives Maomao a hairpin
Xiaolan (小蘭): Maomao's friend among the palace servants
Basen (馬閃): Gaoshun's second son and an attendant of Jinshi
text: The twelve characters of this quiz run from Maomao and Jinshi to the four high-ranking consorts and the people around them.
excerpt: The freckled adopted daughter of an apothecary and doctor named Luomen who lives in the red-light district of the capital city.
